canonical_name: The ring of integers of a number field is a Dedekind domain
canonical_statement: For every number field K, its ring of integers (the integral closure of the integers in K) is a Dedekind domain.

canonical_formal_target.declaration_or_expression: IsDedekindDomain (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) (candidate shape; exact identifiers unverified)

domain_and_universes: K is a characteristic-zero finite extension of the rational numbers; the exact Lean universe and typeclass binder order remain to be elaborated
quantifiers: number-field structure on K (exact Lean typeclass spelling deferred)
hypotheses: K is a field of characteristic zero
conclusion: The integral closure of Z in K is a Dedekind domain

definitions_and_scope.number_field: A finite field extension of Q, not an arbitrary field or arbitrary algebraic extension
definitions_and_scope.ring_of_integers: The elements of K integral over Z, with their induced commutative-ring structure
definitions_and_scope.dedekind_domain: The full repository/mathlib predicate, not merely unique factorization of nonzero ideals or one selected characterization

excluded_degenerate_cases: The zero ring and fields not finite over Q are outside the claim. Degree-one K = Q remains in scope as a boundary case.
